After Shenyang fell many officials looked to Xiong Tingbi to save Liaodong, but Supervising Secretary Guo Gong alone blamed Tingbi for losing the army and asked that Grand Secretary Liu Yijing be punished as well.

After Shenyang fell, many court officials thought of Xiong Tingbi, but Supervising Secretary Guo Gong alone blamed Tingbi for losing the army and misleading the state, and asked that Grand Secretary Liu Yijing be punished as well.
朝士多思熊廷弼 means many at court thought of Tingbi; 喪師誤國 also includes misleading the state, and ‘save Liaodong’ is not in the Chinese.
The deadlock was not over strategy itself—whether to attack or hold—but over the feud between the frontier commanders, the circuit intendant and the grand coordinator.
It was not that opinions on fighting and defending disagreed, but that the opinions of those who sided with the commissioner or the coordinator disagreed.

棄廣寧遁 is abandoning Guangning and fleeing, not surrendering the city.

Bingqian's outrage only deepened. Because Geng Ruqi, Director of the Bureau of Military Appointments, had echoed Heming and vigorously aided Huazhen in driving out Tingbi, causing the loss of the frontier, he submitted successive memorials attacking them.

王給事中 / Supervising Secretary Wang is treated as Wang Rujian (p029) from the 如堅 sequence; the memorial never restates the surname.
Surnames 左, 周, and 黃 grouped with Yang Lian are not given personal names in this chunk; p055-p057 record them as surname-only fellow-sufferers.
Man Chaojian is praised retrospectively without restated career dates in this chunk.
Jiang Bingqian and Hou Zhenyang are praised retrospectively without restated career dates in this chunk.
